The test image shows corn plants with extensive mosaic mottling -- irregular patches of light green/yellow and dark green across multiple leaves. This is the hallmark of Maize dwarf mosaic virus: mosaic patches of light and dark green with streaks along leaf veins. The plants appear mature but with widespread chlorotic mottling across nearly all visible leaves. This pattern is distinct from downy mildew (parallel white stripes), MCDV (vein banding with stunting), and Stewart's wilt (streaks from flea beetle feeding scars).
